implementationPlan.description:
TDD, RED FIRST: create `packages/benchmark/src/pre-freeze-spec-source.ts` — the pinned-bytes gate and the token/location primitives.
IT TAKES THE SPEC BYTES AS AN INPUT AND VERIFIES THEIR SHA-256 AGAINST THE PIN BEFORE PARSING ANYTHING. Refuse SPEC_BYTES_UNPINNED on mismatch. This is what satisfies rail 0's "never substitute a fixture as the production authority" — no fixture can hash to A62 unless it IS the spec, so the hash gate makes substitution structurally impossible. Do NOT hard-code the absolute out-of-repo path into a production module: the spec lives outside the repo at D:/projexts/moes under epic rail 1, and a hard-coded host path is untestable and unportable. A thin caller resolves the path; this module stays pure.
Primitives it provides: line-accurate tokenisation with exact source locations; extraction of `CORE-I<n>`, `CORE-S<n>`, `BENCH-S<n>`, `G-*` gate IDs and `Section N` pointers; and RANGE EXPANSION.
RANGE EXPANSION IS THE HEART OF THIS MODULE AND THE EASIEST THING TO GET SILENTLY WRONG. The spec writes `CORE-I1…CORE-I22` as a RANGE, not as 22 uses — measured, only CORE-I1 and CORE-I22 appear as literal tokens. The parser must expand a range to its full member set and must never treat an endpoint pair as full coverage. It must also handle BOTH spellings: the ELLIPSIS character (…) at spec:64 and :85, and `..` at spec:407. A parser that understands only `..` under-counts and reports a false PASS. Test both spellings explicitly.
Read as UTF-8 and hash the RAW BYTES exactly as read — a CRLF/LF normalisation before hashing changes the digest and shifts every reported line offset.

HASH GATE. `readPinnedSource(bytes, expectedSha256)` hashes with node:crypto and refuses SPEC_BYTES_UNPINNED (line 0, token = the observed digest) before decoding. THE PIN IS A PARAMETER, not baked in: production passes PINNED_BENCHMARK_SPEC_SHA256 (nothing but those bytes can satisfy it), a test may open a synthetic document by handing in ITS OWN true digest. implementationPlan.description:
TDD, RED FIRST: create `packages/benchmark/src/pre-freeze-reference-audit.ts` — DoD 1, the reference lint the spec itself calls for at spec:8 ("Non-gate pointers use section numbers and are checked by a pre-freeze reference lint (every `Section N` resolves to the intended title)").
THIS IS A CROSS-DOCUMENT CHECK AND THAT IS THE WHOLE DESIGN. BENCH-S1..14 are defined AND used inside the benchmark, so their bidirectional equality is in-file. CORE-I1..22 and CORE-S1..14 are NOT: the benchmark cites them only as ranges and states at spec:64 that it "CONSUMES those artifacts; it never redefines them". Their definitions live in the design, which carries 22 distinct CORE-I and 14 distinct CORE-S tokens and hashes to epic rail 1's pin. So the audit takes BOTH documents' bytes, each hash-gated, and asserts the ranges the benchmark cites are exactly the set the design defines.
Assert bidirectionally in both directions and ASSERT THE CASE COUNT for each family — 22, 14, 14, and 20 gate IDs. Rail 1 says zero generated cases are a failure, and a sweep over the 2 literal CORE-I tokens would PASS while testing nothing. The count assertion is what makes the sweep falsifiable.
Also required by DoD 1: REJECT EVERY AMBIGUOUS BARE S/I TOKEN — a bare `S3` or `I7` with no CORE-/BENCH- prefix is REFERENCE_AMBIGUOUS, because the same bare number means different things in the two families. And enforce spec:8's convention: gates are ALWAYS cited by gate ID and NEVER by section number, so a gate referenced positionally is a defect. Every refusal carries its exact source location.

CITATION CONVENTIONS. Bare `S3`/`I3` -> REFERENCE_AMBIGUOUS with exact location; a gate cited positionally ("the acceptance gate in Section 0") -> REFERENCE_AMBIGUOUS carrying the offending phrase, per spec:8's "always cited by that ID, never by section number". Section pointers resolve to numbered headings; the module states plainly that "resolves to the intended TITLE" is outside mechanical reach rather than implying it checked intent.

ONE PRODUCTION DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED BY A RED, worth recording because it is the exact shape rail 1 warns about: the gate-ID tokeniser was narrowed to the twenty known IDs, so an INVENTED gate `G-L9` was INVISIBLE rather than unresolved - the roster check cannot refuse what the tokeniser never emits, and that arm would have been vacuous forever. `GATE_ID` is now `/G-[A-Za-z0-9]+(?:-[A-Za-z0-9]+)*/g`: tokenise permissively, validate against the transcribed roster. Verified the broad pattern still yields exactly the 20 on the real spec.

SWEEP_ZERO_CASES is emitted PER FAMILY plus globally, so a document with no tokens refuses four times and can never report ok.

implementationPlan.description:
TDD, RED FIRST: create `packages/benchmark/src/pre-freeze-gate-audit.ts` — DoD 2, the semantic half. Five checks, each with its own arm and its own code:
  (a) RUNG-TO-GATE INVENTORIES IDENTICAL. Every gate reachable from a rung appears in the rung's inventory and vice versa, across L1..L5, compared against step 2's transcribed roster of twenty.
  (b) EXHAUSTIVE THREE-VALUED HANDLING WITH PRECEDENCE. Every gate defines PASS, FAIL and UNKNOWN. Assert spec:85's explicit rule directly, including the co-occurrence case: "Absence-of-evidence ⇒ UNKNOWN; evidence-of-defect ⇒ FAIL. Precedence when both co-occur: FAIL dominates." Rail 2 forbids UNKNOWN ever becoming PASS — arm that too.
  (c) COMPARATOR-INDEXED GATES OVER A NONZERO MODEL-MATCHED COMPARABLE SET. G-L4-quality[m], G-L4-accept[m], G-L5-accept[m], G-L5-cost[m] and G-L5-effort[m] each carry a member index and are AND-ed across the cohort as an intersection-union test (spec:88-89). The cohort floor is `C_min` >= 4 (spec:51). A zero-member cohort must refuse COMPARATOR_INDEX_MISSING, never vacuously pass.
  (d) EVERY LOAD-BEARING THRESHOLD RESOLVES THROUGH THE FROZEN CONSTANTS TABLE (Section 0). spec:8 states every threshold is "a symbol resolved once in the Frozen Constants Table ... including fixed conventional literals (significance level, latency targets, schedule count, reading rate), which are table symbols so the 'unset ⇒ UNKNOWN' guard covers them". An unresolved symbol is CONSTANT_UNRESOLVED. Include the CORE ScheduleCoverageManifest floor: `N_sched` >= 10,000 AND >= the CORE manifest's frozen minima, with the manifest governing (spec:43). ADD A NAMED ARM FOR THE MARGIN TRAP the spec calls out at :88 — acceptance NI uses `M_accept_x`, "never the fan-out `M_accept`"; a gate resolving the wrong symbol is a defect.
  (e) CI TAIL MATCHES ENDPOINT WORSE-DIRECTION, spec:445 item 6: higher-is-better endpoints (acceptance) bound the LOWER tail; worse-is-higher endpoints (cost, failure-rate, overhead) bound the UPPER tail. The spec says a mismatch "is a freeze-blocking defect (this is the check that would have caught the acceptance-gate sign inversion)" — a REAL historical defect. Make catching that inversion an explicit named arm, since it is the single most valuable thing this audit does.
Split into a second module if the per-file cap is approached; (a)-(b) and (c)-(e) divide cleanly.
implementationPlan.note:
SPLIT AS THE STEP AUTHORISES, on the (a)-(b) / (c)-(e) line: `pre-freeze-gate-audit.ts` 234 lines, `pre-freeze-threshold-audit.ts` 239 lines. Every production file in this row is under the 250 target. Package now `Test Files 12 passed (12)` / `Tests 136 passed (136)`; `typecheck` exit 0 with the `$ tsc --project tsconfig.json` echo as execution evidence.

(a) RUNG INVENTORIES - THREE-WAY, not two. `parseReportBlock` reads the Section 1 ladder rows, the Section 12 inventory lines (expanding `(L3 gates)`/`(L4 gates)` back-references and stripping `[umbrella alias ...]` / `[G-expand is out-of-ladder]` while KEEPING `[m]`), and the 18 GATE RESULTS rules. The cumulative ladder closure, the parsed inventory and the transcribed roster must all agree. On real bytes: 5 ladder rows, 5 inventories, 18 gate rules, 6 of them indexed, ZERO refusals. Armed: inventory drops a gate the ladder still wires -> GATE_INVENTORY_MISMATCH "L3"; ladder wires `G-L9` -> refused; a gate cited positionally inside an inventory -> refused with token "Section 7"; a defined gate no rung wires and that is not out-of-ladder -> refused by name. Unparseable input -> SPEC_UNPARSEABLE, never an audit of a document with no ladder.

(b) TRIVALENCE, prose AND behaviour. Five document clauses each with their own arm and their own deletion test: the PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN verdict domain, the any-UNKNOWN arm, the any-FAIL arm, spec:85's "FAIL dominates" precedence, and the never-PASS guard. `resolveRungVerdict` is the PRODUCTION surface implementing the rule, swept exhaustively over all 3^3 = 27 combinations with the case count asserted; UNKNOWN never reaches PASS and an EMPTY verdict list resolves UNKNOWN, because `[].every(isPass)` is `true` and that is how "no member ran, therefore PASS" gets written by accident.

(c) COMPARATOR COVERAGE over SIX gates. Empty cohort -> COMPARATOR_INDEX_MISSING "COMPARABLE cohort" plus SWEEP_ZERO_CASES, generatedCases 0, verdict UNKNOWN, ok false - it cannot vacuously pass. Cohort of 3 -> refused at "C_min". Full cohort of 4 -> 24 generated cases, verdict PASS. One hole in the per-member table -> COMPARATOR_INDEX_MISSING "G-L5-cost[member-3]" and the cohort resolves UNKNOWN, not PASS. One member FAIL dominates a co-occurring UNKNOWN.

(d) CONSTANTS. Section 0's table is parsed within its own heading bounds (a document-wide backtick scan would swallow every gate ID) and yields exactly the transcribed 38 symbols. Each gate's report rule must NAME its entitled symbol in either spelling via the ASCII<->Greek map, matched with word boundaries. Armed: `G-UI` consuming the inline literal "500 ms" instead of `L_UI` -> CONSTANT_UNRESOLVED "G-UI:L_UI". THE FAN-OUT MARGIN TRAP has its own arm: swapping `M_accept_x` for `M_accept` in `G-L5-accept` refuses BOTH "G-L5-accept:M_accept" (forbidden symbol present) and "G-L5-accept:M_accept_x" (entitled symbol absent) - word boundaries are load-bearing, since `M_accept` is a prefix of `M_accept_x`. N_sched floor armed three ways: dropping 10,000, losing "manifest governs", losing the ScheduleCoverageManifest reference.

(e) CI TAIL - the historical sign inversion, and the single most valuable arm here. Seven non-inferiority gates, case count asserted equal to the roster size. Flipping `G-L4-accept[m]` to bound the UPPER tail refuses CI_TAIL_DIRECTION_WRONG token "G-L4-accept:UPPER" at line 414; flipping `G-L5-cost[m]` to the lower tail refuses "G-L5-cost:LOWER"; a gate that states no tail at all refuses "G-overhead:tail-unstated" rather than passing silently. Mutants are built by rewriting one line of the REAL spec IN MEMORY and re-opening it under its OWN digest - the external documents are never touched.

TWO ROSTER CORRECTIONS FORCED BY REAL REDS, both recorded in the roster file: (1) `rubric_weights` removed from G-L4-quality - it IS load-bearing but the link is declared table-side at spec:41, not in the gate's rule, so listing it refused the pinned document for a defect it does not have; (2) `N_sched` removed from G-L1 - the Section 1 ladder rule states it and the Section 12 report line does not; it keeps its own dedicated arm. The roster now means exactly "what each gate's REPORT LINE must name".

ONE PRODUCTION DEFECT FOUND BY A RED, the subtlest of this row: `ruleTextFor` originally concatenated the gate's report line WITH its rung's ladder row. That looked harmless and was not - the L4 ladder row carries the spec's OWN warning "never the fan-out `M_accept`" and the L5 row carries `M_accept_x` as prose, so the widened rule (i) refused the pinned document for a margin defect it does not have and (ii) HID a real margin swap behind the neighbouring text, leaving the trap arm permanently green. Narrowed to the report line only.
